title: Factor Trinomials
student_objective: I can factor quadratic trinomials over the real numbers, including perfect-square trinomials, and identify when real factors are not possible.
teacher_objective: Diagnose greatest-common-factor, factor-pair, sign, nonmonic grouping, perfect-square, real-factor, verification, and contextual-model errors.

concept_cards.title: Factor out the GCF first
concept_cards.content: Before factoring the remaining trinomial, extract the greatest factor shared by every term.

concept_cards.title: For x²+bx+c, use sum and product
concept_cards.content: Find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b. They become the constants in the two binomial factors.

concept_cards.title: For ax²+bx+c, split the middle term
concept_cards.content: Find two numbers with product ac and sum b, split bx, then factor by grouping.

concept_cards.title: Recognize perfect squares
concept_cards.content: a²+2ab+b²=(a+b)² and a²-2ab+b²=(a-b)². The middle term determines the sign.

concept_cards.title: Verify and check real-factor possibility
concept_cards.content: Multiply the factors to recover the original trinomial. If b²-4ac is negative, the quadratic has no real linear factors.

items.tutor_behavior: Find two integers with product 12 and sum 7.

items.prompt: Factor 3x²+6x by first finding the greatest common factor.
items.tutor_behavior: Every term contains 3x; extract it before doing anything else.

items.prompt: Is x²+10x+25 a perfect-square trinomial? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Check whether 25=5² and 10x=2(x)(5).

solution_steps.explanation: The constants must have opposite signs because their product is negative.
Choose the pair whose sum is the middle coefficient.
Write the two binomial factors and verify by multiplication.

items.tutor_behavior: Use product -12 and sum -1; do not choose signs from the constant alone.

solution_steps.explanation: Find numbers with product 18 and sum 11.
Split the middle term using 9x and 2x.

items.tutor_behavior: Use the ac method and make the grouped binomial factors match.

solution_steps.explanation: Both outside terms are perfect squares.
The middle term matches the negative perfect-square pattern.

items.tutor_behavior: Check both square terms and the signed double product.
Find a factor pair of -15 with sum 2.

items.prompt: Use the X method for 2x²+7x+3. The side numbers are 6 and 1. Divide BOTH side numbers by a=2. What two reduced values do you get? Enter both values; order does not matter.
items.answer_placeholder: Enter both reduced values, e.g. 3 and 1/2

solution_steps.explanation: Divide the first X-side number by a=2.
Divide the second X-side number by a=2.
After reducing, use the denominator as the x-coefficient and the numerator as the constant.
These are the final factors of 2x²+7x+3.

items.tutor_behavior: At this step, do not enter the final factors yet. Divide BOTH X-side numbers by a=2: 6÷2 and 1÷2. Enter the two reduced values.
Extract 2 first; the remaining trinomial is a perfect square.
Use product 20 and sum 9.
A positive constant and negative middle coefficient require two negative constants.
Use ac=-15 and split -14x into x-15x.
Extract 5, then recognize x²+4x+4 as a perfect square.
Use product -24 and sum -5.
Use ac=-12 and split -x into 3x-4x.
Verify 9x² and 16 are squares and 24x is their positive double product.

items.prompt: A student factors x²+6x+8 as (x+2)(x-4). Is the student correct?
items.explanation_prompt: Explain how the sum and product reveal the error, then give the correct factorization.
items.explanation_guidance: The constants must multiply to 8 and add to 6. The pair 2 and 4 works, so x²+6x+8=(x+2)(x+4).
items.tutor_behavior: Require both the sum-product check and the corrected factors.

items.prompt: A rectangle has area x²+7x+10. Write possible binomial expressions for its length and width.
items.tutor_behavior: Factor the area polynomial and interpret the factors as dimensions.
Use product 15 and sum 8.
Use product -35 and sum -2.
Use ac=20 and split 12x into 10x+2x.
Use ac=120 and split -22x into -10x-12x.
Extract -1 so the leading coefficient becomes positive, then factor the perfect square.

items.prompt: Can x²+4x+8 be factored into real linear factors? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Compute b²-4ac=16-32=-16; a negative discriminant means no real zeros or real linear factors.

items.prompt: Factor over the real numbers: x²+2x-1.
items.tutor_behavior: Complete the square or use the quadratic formula to find zeros -1±√2, then write x-r for each factor.

items.prompt: Multiply (x-6)(x+2) to verify the factorization of x²-4x-12.
items.tutor_behavior: Multiply all four partial products and combine -6x+2x.

items.prompt: The area of a garden is 2x²+9x+10. Factor the expression to give possible dimensions.
items.tutor_behavior: Factor the area polynomial, then interpret the binomials as dimensions.

items.prompt: Which pattern identifies x²-14x+49 as a perfect-square trinomial?
items.tutor_behavior: Match the expression to a²-2ab+b² with a=x and b=7.
Extract 3, then factor 4x²-9 as a difference of squares.

items.prompt: A trinomial has a=1, b=5, and c=9. Does it have real linear factors? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: The discriminant is 5²-4(1)(9)=-11, so there are no real linear factors.

factor_pairs.teacher_signal: Chooses factors with the correct product but wrong sum

gcf_first.teacher_signal: Leaves a common factor in the trinomial or stops before factoring completely

perfect_square.teacher_signal: Checks only the outside squares or uses the wrong middle-term sign

sign_reasoning.teacher_signal: Assigns factor signs without checking both sum and product

nonmonic_grouping.teacher_signal: Uses c instead of ac or creates nonmatching grouped binomials

verification.teacher_signal: Does not multiply factors to recover the original trinomial

real_factor_check.teacher_signal: Claims real factors without checking the discriminant or real zeros

context_factorization.teacher_signal: Factors correctly but does not connect factors to contextual quantities
